newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says its foreign reserves now $5.03 bln.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says its foreign reserves now $5.03 bln.

text.p: Nigeria's external reserves have increased to $5.03 billion by end-February from $4.086 billion in December 1996, Finance Minister Anthony Ani said.

Ani, speaking in southeastern Uyo town at the weekend and quoted by the state news agency, said proper management of available resources and the positive effects of government's fiscal policy were responsible for the 25 percent rise in the reserves.
According to Ani, a tight fiscal spending policy introduced by military ruler General Sani Abacha since 1995 helped reduce the country's current external debts to $28 billion from $32.5 billion.
In addition, the appreciation of the Japanese yen over the dollar aided the debt reduction because part of Nigeria's external debt was denominated in yen, he said.
Economic experts believed the indebted African nation has been able to accumulate such external reserves largely due to last year's high prices of crude oil, Nigeria's main export commodity.
The experts say Nigeria seems to be building up its foreign reserves with the ultimate aim of making its naira currency, which now exchanges largely in a free rate, convertible.
Ani said the devaluation of the naira to 85 naira to the dollar three weeks ago was aimed at checking the activities of illegal currency operators in the country.
"They buy the naira at 80 naira to the dollar from at the AFEM (autonomous foreign exchange market) rate and turn round to sell same at 84 naira in the black market," he said.
Nigeria operates a dual exchange rate in the AFEM where forex is sold weekly and settles its official debts and other government transactions at a rate of 22 naira to the dollar.
